Bill Lucas also caught Rowe close home and so gained second place. In the Field Events Syd Jones won the Weight with 38ft. 4in., and showed he is fast getting back to his pre-war performances.

We have the talent, some of it already shown, some of it dormant, but to mention only these few names is to comment on a strength which could do much: Broadbent, Botwright, Burfitt, Blowfield, Nankeville, Marchant, Herbert, Read, Lucas, Stimpson.

Owing to sickness there were many notable absentees including both the Herbert's, both the Lucas's and Frank Abberton. The field was led out by Tom Carter but was well together when at 2 miles Carter went into the lead.

Jack Brown, the holder, was a non-starter, but a small bunch of runners soon detached themselves from the rest of the field with Lucas, Herbert, Tooby, Bromley, Stokell, Bruce and Stearman more or less together.
Walker allowed Green to hand over with him at the end of the third stage, but Archie Bedford, Eddie Short and Bill Lucas saw to it that we maintained our unbeaten record for this race.

Chas Walker, although suffering from the after-effects of a cold, ran a good first "leg" which was inside the previous lap record time, held by Bill Lucas, but even so could only hand over in second place to Cook, of Hadleigh A.C.

Walker just beat Eddie Short for second place, and then came Jack Braughton 5th, Bill Lucas 7th, Archie Bedford 9th and Len Herbert 11th. All the first five were selected to run for Surrey in the Inter-Counties race at York, and Jack Brown 7th in the Kent race and A.
Walker put in a really fine run to put them in the lead on the 3rd stage, and this was maintained by Wright, Short, Lucas and Bedford down to the end of the 7th relay.

Carter, Footer, Penny, Herbert, Green, Scrimshaw, Lucas and Stimpson were no more endowed than some of our present men; they merely exploited their gifts more by plenty of hard training and by turning out regularly in all Club matches.
Cry-God for Lucas!

He ran a clever race, using his head as well as his legs, and in perfect style came away in the last mile to win comfortably ... Lucas, a newcomer, ran well in his first important race in our colours. THE ENGLISH CROSS COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIP .....

Early in April a 27 strong field tackled the 5 mile road run where experience, in the shape of Arthur Penny, triumphed over men who were to make their names over the coming years – Lucas, Len and Eric Herbert, and one who became “Mr Athletics” himself, Les Cohen.
